title: Making and Documenting Assumptions
description: Learn how to make reasonable assumptions when requirements are incomplete, and how to document them clearly.

data.text: Real-world requirements are rarely complete. In an interview, the problem statement is intentionally vague. Making explicit assumptions turns unknowns into design inputs and shows the interviewer that you can operate with incomplete information.

data.title: State Assumptions Out Loud
data.text: Write or say each assumption clearly. Hidden assumptions lead to misaligned designs and lost points.

data.title: Typical Interview Assumptions
items: Assume a reasonable number of daily active users when scale is not given.
Assume eventual consistency for non-critical data unless told otherwise.
Assume a standard deployment in a single cloud region for simplicity.
Assume human-generated content for moderation and spam considerations.

data.text: Keep a running list of assumptions on your whiteboard or document. Number them so you can reference them later. If the interviewer corrects an assumption, update your design in real time. This demonstrates adaptability and attention to detail.

data.caption: How assumptions flow into the design process.
data.definition:
flowchart TD
    A[Incomplete Problem] --> B[Identify Gaps]
    B --> C[Make Explicit Assumptions]
    C --> D[Document Assumptions]
    D --> E[Design with Assumptions]
    E --> F[Review with Interviewer]

data.title: Assumption Best Practices
points: Document them so you can reference them later.
Update your design if the interviewer corrects an assumption.
Use assumptions to unblock design decisions quickly.
data.takeaway: Good assumptions keep the design moving forward while showing thoughtful judgment.
